title: IDTM Dismantling Description
overview: This document describes all dismantling steps for the IDTM (Infectious Disease Treatment Module) based on the AZF4-27 Inflatable Tent system. The IDTM consists of 3 tents (2 patient pods + 1 staff pod) with 6 vestibules, hard flooring, and sun shadowing nets. Dismantling consists of repeating the installation procedure in reverse order.

sections.title: Pre-Dismantling Requirements
sections.description: Required conditions and safety warnings before dismantling

requirements.title: Personnel Requirements
content: 2-3 persons minimum for safe dismantling
Training recommended for all personnel

requirements.title: Weather Requirements
content: Dismantling is strongly discouraged in case of strong winds or heavy rains
Wind: Maximum 40 km/h during dismantling

requirements.title: Safety and Preparation Warnings
content: Ensure all accessories have been removed from inside the tent
Clean the groundsheet to ensure no sharp objects (stones, branches, etc.) are left inside
Sharp objects could damage the tent during storage
Do not drag tent covers over the ground - this may damage the tent skin
Roof covers are easy to fold - if you notice any resistance stop folding and check for blockages
Avoid packing the tent when it is wet, humid and/or dirty
If you pack the tent whilst still wet or humid, unpack, clean and dry it within 72 hours to avoid mildew
Collect, clean and pack all items, and run an inventory before loading onto the truck

sections.title: Electrical System Removal
sections.description: Remove electrical system and lighting before dismantling

steps.title: Remove Electrical System
steps.purpose: Disconnect and pack all electrical components
actions: Disconnect all LED stripe feeders
Remove master and slave dimmers
Disconnect LED strips from tent arches
Collect all extension cables
Remove splitters
Pack main distribution box
Store all electrical components in designated boxes

sections.title: Cleaning and Preparation
sections.description: Clean and dry all tents before dismantling

steps.title: Clean and Dry Tents
steps.purpose: Prevent mildew and damage during storage
actions: Remove all accessories from inside the tent
Clean the groundsheet thoroughly
Remove all sharp objects (stones, branches, debris)
Ensure tent is completely dry
If tent is wet when packing, must unpack and dry within 72 hours to avoid mildew
steps.criticalWarning: All items should be cleaned and fully dried before being stored. Wet or humid tents packed for more than 72 hours will develop mildew.

sections.title: Remove Anchoring System
sections.description: Remove all pegs and guy ropes

steps.title: Remove Guy Ropes and Pegs
actions: Remove all guy ropes from vestibules and main tents
Extract all 50cm T-pegs from ground
Extract all 30cm T-pegs from groundsheet loops
Clean all pegs
Place pegs and ropes in their corresponding bags
Total pegs to remove: approximately 84 pegs

sections.title: Remove Inner Cabins
sections.description: Disassemble and pack inner cabin structures

steps.title: Disconnect Inner Cabins
actions: Starting from one side, disconnect toggle buttons from plastic studs
Move along the arches removing all toggle buttons
Continue until all toggle buttons are disconnected
Remove inner cabin liners from tent

steps.title: Remove Support Bars
actions: Remove all support bars from patient pods (4 bars each)
Remove all support bars from staff pod (2 bars)
Store bars appropriately

steps.title: Fold and Pack Inner Cabins
actions: Fold inner cabins on a clean surface or over plastic sheeting
Ensure fabric is clean and dry
Place folded inner cabins in their corresponding bags
Secure bags properly

steps.title: Disconnect Vestibules from Main Tents
actions: Disconnect all locking pins/bolts connecting vestibule spacers to tents
Remove double stud connections from single studs
Separate all 6 vestibules from main tent structures

sections.title: Tents and Vestibules Deflation
sections.description: Deflate all tent structures and prepare for folding

steps.title: Prepare for Deflation
actions: Close all windows on main tents and vestibules
Leave tent doors OPEN so air doesn't get trapped during deflation
Disconnect pressure monitoring system from inflator
Remove pressure feedback tube from inside tent
Open protective caps on inflation valves
Insert finger inside valve and turn central pin counterclockwise with nail
Open all inflation valves to let air out
Wait for tents to deflate naturally
steps.criticalNote: Leave tent doors OPEN during deflation to prevent air from getting trapped inside and to prevent damage to air passage valves.

steps.title: Facilitate Tent Collapse
steps.purpose: Help tent deflate properly for easier folding
actions: Press on the arches at waist level to help tent collapse onto itself
Ensure roof falls on top of groundsheet (not sideways)
Take inflator from bag
Connect inflation hose manifold to INLET coupling (deflation mode)
steps.criticalNote: To facilitate ensuing folding process, press on arches so roof falls on top of groundsheet and not sideways.

steps.title: Complete Deflation with Inflator
steps.purpose: Empty tent frame completely for easier folding
actions: Once tent is deflated, insert inflation hose taps in inflation valves
Fasten screw rings and open taps
Connect all inflation valves to hoses
Turn inflator ON in deflation mode (INLET)
Wait approximately 5 minutes for complete deflation
When tent frame is fully deflated, turn inflator OFF
Remove hose taps from valves
Close all inflation valves
steps.criticalNote: Use of inflator in deflation mode (INLET) is very important as it helps empty the tent frame completely and greatly simplifies the ensuing folding procedure.

steps.title: Position Deflated Tent
actions: Adjust position of tent roof so it sits on top of groundsheet
Place guy ropes on top of tent roof
Ensure tent is properly positioned for folding

images.description: Tent folding pattern diagram - flat panel
Tent folding pattern diagram - wedge/edge piece

steps.title: Remove Sun Shadowing Nets and Spacers
actions: Remove all 3 sun shadowing nets from tents
Deflate pneumatic spacers
Disconnect spacers from tent couplings
Remove locking pins/bolts
Fold sun shadowing nets
Place nets in their corresponding bags

sections.title: Tent Folding and Packing
sections.description: Fold and pack tents for storage and transport

steps.title: Fold Tents According to Pattern
actions: Follow folding pattern as shown in manual diagrams
Fold tent into rectangular bundle
Ensure width matches transport bag width

steps.title: Clean Tent During Folding
actions: Ensure tent is clean before packing
Remove gravels and stones beneath groundsheet while folding
Sharp objects will damage tent cover during storage
steps.criticalWarning: Make sure tent is clean when you fold and pack it. Gravels and stones will damage the tent cover during storage.

steps.title: Verify Tent is Dry
actions: Ensure tent is completely dry when folding and packing
If tent is wet when packed, must install again later in warehouse to clean and dry
Prepare for proper storage only when fully dry
steps.criticalWarning: Make sure the tent is dry when you fold and pack it. If wet when packed, you should install it again later in your warehouse to clean it and let it dry as preparation for storage.

steps.title: Roll Tent Bundle
actions: Roll the resulting bundle starting from opposite side of transport bag
Fold one end of resulting bundle
Place tent transport bag beneath folded end
Fold bundle back onto the bag

steps.title: Verify Bundle Width
steps.purpose: Ensure proper fit in transport bag
actions: Before starting to roll tent bundle, check width matches bag width
Adjust folding if necessary to match bag dimensions

steps.title: Secure Packed Tent
actions: Ensure bundle is well centered in the bag
Close bag using provided straps
Tighten straps securely
Verify tent is properly packaged

sections.title: Hard Floor Dismantling
sections.description: Remove and pack hard floor tiles

steps.title: Disassemble Hard Floor
actions: Remove hard floor tiles in reverse order of installation
Stack tiles carefully on pallet
Use pallet truck to move tiles pallet to storage area
Weight per pallet: approximately 180 kg - use appropriate lifting equipment

sections.title: Final Inventory and Packing
sections.description: Complete dismantling process with inventory and organization

steps.title: Inventory and Organization
steps.purpose: Ensure all components are accounted for and properly stored
actions: Collect all components and verify against packing list
Clean all items before packing
Check for packing labels and replace missing labels if needed
Ensure packaging units haven't been damaged during dismantling
Pack most sensitive items on top (e.g. lights)
Ensure no item can fall during transport or storage
Run complete inventory before loading onto truck
Verify all 3 main tents are packed
Verify all 6 vestibules are packed
Verify all inner cabins are packed
Verify all electrical components are packed
Verify hard floor tiles are on pallet
Verify all pegs, ropes, and accessories are in bags

requirements.title: Storage Requirements
content: All items must be stored in adequate packaging, away from water and vermin
All items must be cleaned and fully dried before storage
Ideal storage temperature: 18-21°C
Air humidity: 60-65%
Storage area should have good air circulation
No vermin should enter storage area
Items should be stored away from water sources
Most sensitive items should be packed on top
Ensure no item can fall during transport or storage

requirements.title: Maintenance Before Storage
content: Clean all textile parts according to cleaning instructions
Clean special stains from grass, oil, ballpoint pens, etc.
Visually inspect all textile parts for cuts, holes, abrasions, tears
Check open seams or welded joints for damage
Identify broken parts that need replacement
Check all moving parts like zippers by opening and closing them
Look for broken or corroded parts
Check bags visually for any damage
Ensure all parts are dry before packing
Repack all clean, repaired and complete units on correct pallets
